## Servers

- **One server per tree, however many assistants use it.** Over stdio, `serve` now relays to a backend for the tree on a Unix socket in the per-user state directory (directory `0700`, socket `0600`) and starts it when none runs. The backend holds the graph, the watcher and the sleep, and answers every client. Several assistants on one tree build and watch it once; a connection a client forgets to close costs a few megabytes and no polling.
- The backend accepts connections before it reads the tree, so a client connects at once. A lock lets one client start it while the others wait, a socket left by a backend that died is replaced, and a client whose backend went away starts a new one and sends the request again.
- The backend ends a minute after its last client leaves (`--linger <seconds>`). Backends are keyed by version, tree and options, so an upgrade never talks to an older one. `--own-process` keeps a server per client; Windows always does.

## Releases

- The Homebrew tap and the Scoop bucket move only once the release is published. A release that failed after its build left them naming archives that did not exist.

## Install

- Homebrew: `brew install attackwave/glasir/glasir`
- Scoop: add the bucket `Attackwave/scoop-glasir`, then run `scoop install glasir`
